Subject: Initial ask — privacy pathway for HealthConnect onboarding

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are evaluating Redwood for text extraction and triage in our urgent care network. Before we can go deeper, our legal and security teams need a short feasibility assessment that covers the combined requirements across HIPAA (BAA), GLBA (customer financial data flows), and FERPA (student records in our partnered school clinics).

Concretely, can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can sign a BAA and accommodate a customer-managed KMS for PHI keys (we prefer CMEK)
- What subprocessor residency options you offer for US-only hosting and whether any EU/APAC subprocessors are in the call chain
- If you have sample GLBA language or a GLBA addendum and how transaction-level logs/audit trails are surfaced to customers
- Any known conflicts between your streaming API (KV cache) and FERPA restrictions for student PII retention

I've attached our standard security questionnaire (PDF) and an example BAA we use internally — want to see what gaps you expect. Can we get a two-week turnaround on a feasibility note and an initial artifact package? Also propose a 30-minute working sync later this week if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Sanchez
Security & Privacy Manager
HealthConnect

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 9:18 AM Elena Sanchez <elena.sanchez@healthconnect.org> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo last week...

Thanks for the forward. Quick read and notes below (high-level assessment).

1) BAA / HIPAA: we can sign a BAA. For PHI in hosted Redwood, standard BAA covers storage, processing and breach notification. For CMEK: our Private (on-prem / VPC) and Dedicated offerings support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration — we need to confirm whether their KMS is AWS KMS or another provider. Action: request KMS provider + key management access model.

2) GLBA: GLBA usually requires explicit contractual commitments around safeguarding consumer financial information and auditability. We do not currently publish a GLBA addendum as a separate template, but we can provide GLBA-specific clauses to append to the DPA/contract. We need to confirm what specific financial data classes they consider (transactional details vs. tokenized references). For audit trails: we expose per-request metadata, tokenized traces, and retention settings via our Console and API logs (can produce exported logs for their SIEM). Action: ask for examples of the GLBA data elements and required retention window.

3) FERPA: constraints are usually residency and retention for student PII; FERPA often sits well with Dedicated or Private deployments with US residency. Concern: streaming/continuous KV cache can retain prefixes unless explicitly flushed or configured with short TTL. For FERPA-sensitive inputs we recommend: dedicated route, enforced cache TTL=0 for affected routes, and strict purge policies.

4) Subprocessors / residency: we can provide a subprocessor map and residency matrix. Important to confirm whether they require a contractual ban on any subprocessors (rare) or just US-only processing.

Artifacts we should deliver in a 2-week package:
- Short feasibility memo (1–2 pages) with gap map vs. their attached questionnaire
- Proposed redline snippets for BAA + GLBA clauses + FERPA notes
- Subprocessor/residency matrix and SOC2 evidence (redacted as needed)
- Implementation checklist for CMEK + onboarding steps (ops-runbook)

I can draft the legal snippets and the feasibility memo, Marissa can draft the ops checklist and residency mapping. Timeline: draft out in 7 business days for internal review, final package at 10 business days. If they need legal countersigned BAA sooner, we can accelerate.

Mina Haddad
Director, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few operational items / clarifications from the services side: 

- Residency: for US-only we have two deployment flavors: Dedicated in our US region (multi-tenant but contractually isolated) or Private VPC/on-prem. Dedicated typically satisfies customers that require US processing only; Private if they require network isolation or air-gapped controls.
- KMS: integration time depends on their KMS provider — AWS KMS is fastest (2–3 weeks for key rotation setup + kms-access control review). GCP KMS/other HSMs will take longer.
- Logs & Audit: we can export request + token-level logs to S3/Syslog for their SIEM. For GLBA auditability we recommend a 90–365 day retention spec (they should tell us).
- Cache: for the FERPA routes we can set route-level cache TTL=0 and enable immediate KV purges via API. We'll add a checklist to the ops doc with commands and expected timing (purge within <30s typical).

I'll build an implementation runbook (ops checklist) that includes: deployment option recommendation, KMS integration steps, log export config, cache/TTL controls, and a go/no-go checklist for the pilot. Expect my draft in 5 business days.

Also: Dylan — please capture this as deal HC-2026-1123 in HubSpot and request Elena's KMS provider details and the GLBA data element list. Linking HubSpot record: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/HC-2026-1123
